triggers.grounds: Band is honest and the seam holds at it. The front edge is the ruled F1|M frame seam (rows never straddle 1:1|1:2), so no rival cut exists there. The back edge rests on a tier-1 daughters-address standing in the next verse's own bytes: בְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (oshb:Song.1.5, tier: byte; it collates byte at oshb:Song.1.5 and only skeleton against oshb:Song.3.5, so the row's site-specific splice is the right one), a new addressee absent from the 2ms chain of MT 1:2-1:4. That chain re-derives from the bytes: דֹּדֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Song.1.2), שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ / שְׁמֶ֑ךָ / אֲהֵבֽוּךָ (oshb:Song.1.3), אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ / דֹדֶ֨יךָ֙ / אֲהֵבֽוּךָ (oshb:Song.1.4), all tier: byte. The stated reason for the band -- the enallage vs unmarked-chorus question left unsettled by any single tier-1 form -- is bespoke, true, and matches the book's own pre-registered low-confidence region for 1:2-4; frontier_flag_considered is true. The honest hold on בָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte) as 2fs in form and 2ms only on a pausal reading, with no morphology layer staged, is exactly the posture the band should carry. Confidence is neither over- nor under-stated.

findings.claim: The densest-class superlative names no count object and carries no digit, and it is true only under a per-token density reading.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale asserts that the span's middle verse carries its densest 2ms evidence. Re-derived with the count object named: unambiguous 2ms forms per verse are 1 at MT 1:2 (דֹּדֶ֖יךָ), 3 at MT 1:3 (שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ, שְׁמֶ֑ךָ, אֲהֵבֽוּךָ), and 3 at MT 1:4 (אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ, דֹדֶ֨יךָ֙, אֲהֵבֽוּךָ) -- plus the contested בָּ֔ךְ that the row itself entertains as a pausal 2ms, which would make MT 1:4 four. All splices tier: byte. So under a raw-count reading the claim is a tie or false; under a per-token density reading it is true (3 of 10 tokens at MT 1:3 against 3 of 16 at MT 1:4). Scored as a true-but-undigited universals claim. The staged universals gate does not catch it: the densest lexeme is in its vocabulary, but the tier-word dampener passes the sentence because a byte tier label and oshb:Song.1.3 stand in it -- and that byte cite grounds the three forms at MT 1:3, not the cross-verse comparison the superlative makes. Not load-bearing: the seam rests on the 2ms chain and the MT 1:5 vocative.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair in boundary_rationale: either drop the superlative, or supply the count object and its digits -- e.g. name the per-token density, 3 of 10 tokens at MT 1:3 against 3 of 16 at MT 1:4 -- so the comparison is swept rather than asserted.

findings.claim: The two Hebrew form-claims that carry this row's medium_low band are cited to the WEB rendering instead of the pointed forms standing in the cited verses.
findings.grounds: device_notes argues the opening enallage from a third-masculine verb cited as web:Song.1.2 but does not splice יִשָּׁקֵ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.2, tier: byte), the 3ms form itself; boundary_rationale locates the person shift by a curly-quoted WEB clause at web:Song.1.4 without splicing the 1cp cohortative pair נָגִ֤ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה֙ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte). I re-derived both from the bytes and both claims are TRUE -- this is an engagement and tier shortfall, not a false claim. It matters because the shifting reference is the row's own stated ground for holding at medium_low, and the campaign rule requires the pointed splice with a tier label for every original-language claim. The WEB quotation itself is verbatim with an in-field web: ref (the staged web-quote check returns GREEN).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: add the two pointed splices with tier labels beside the existing WEB citations -- the 3ms form at oshb:Song.1.2 and the 1cp cohortative pair at oshb:Song.1.4 -- leaving the seam argument unchanged.

triggers.grounds: Band is honest and if anything conservative. The front edge rests on a tier-1 address-vocabulary anchor in the opening verse's own bytes, הִנָּ֤ךְ ... רַעְיָתִ֔י (oshb:Song.1.15, tier: byte), answered by הִנְּךָ֨ ... דוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte). The back edge at 2:3|2:4 is the row's declared weakness and it declares it accurately: I confirmed from the bytes that MT 2:4 carries no vocative, no dodi/rayati token and no second-person form, so the same 1cs voice does run past the cut, and the row rests the close on bracket completion rather than on a voice shift -- with the straddling apple-stem link disclosed (word-bound sweep re-run: 4 verses, MT 2:3, MT 2:5, MT 7:9 = WEB 7:8, MT 8:5, in four distinct consonantal spellings, and the MT 7:9 = WEB 7:8 dual is arithmetically right). The ketiv/qere at MT 1:17 falls inside the span and IS disclosed with neither reading claimed (the WLC K/Q inventory holds MT 1:17, 2:11, 2:13, 4:9). The hinnakh/hinnekha skeleton digit re-sweeps to exactly 3 verses (MT 1:15, 1:16, 4:1). An unmarked back seam on a span the book's own granularity ruling pre-names as a whole-held dialogue zone is properly a medium_low, not higher.

findings.claim: The unqualified statement that the opening and closing frames share no run is true only at byte tier; both frames share runs at accent_stripped and skeleton tier.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale (and the identical sentence in the seam-partner row) says the two mirrored pairs are not a byte-identical inclusio and that the opening and closing frames share no run. Collated: רַעְיָתִ֔י (oshb:Song.1.15) against oshb:Song.2.2 returns accent_stripped, and דוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.16) against oshb:Song.2.3 returns skeleton. So the frames do share two runs below byte tier, and those two shared runs -- רַעְיָתִ֖י and דּוֹדִ֖י at the closing end -- are precisely what makes the two pairs a mirror at all. The sentence's own next clause tier-labels the hinnakh/hinnekha skeleton sharing correctly, so the omission is local. The campaign tier-disclosure standard requires every recurrence and non-recurrence claim to be tier-labelled at write time. Not load-bearing: the bracket argument is unaffected and is in fact strengthened by the sharing.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair in boundary_rationale: qualify to share no byte-identical run, and name the accent_stripped sharing of the his-word-for-her token (oshb:Song.1.15 against oshb:Song.2.2) and the skeleton sharing of the her-word-for-him token (oshb:Song.1.16 against oshb:Song.2.3).

findings.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative narrates the chunking schema rather than the text.
findings.grounds: The field's second sentence rejects a sub-verse re-cut as unavailable at row granularity because spans are verse-granular, so Song.2.3 must fall wholly to one side. Row granularity and verse-granular spans describe the deliverable's own schema constraint, not the text; the binding register law is that row prose describes the TEXT, never the process. Recorded honestly as borderline: this phrasing is not in the book strategy's enumerated register bans (decision-ids, section citations, erratum narration, positional row references, file-order talk, reviewer names, tool filenames, staged-file stems), and it is carrying a genuine rival disclosure. Purely cosmetic, with no evidence effect -- the underlying byte facts at oshb:Song.2.3 are correct.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: state the same rival in text register -- that the first-person run of MT 2:3 continues into MT 2:4 while MT 2:3 carries the antiphon's closing anchor -- without naming the row or span apparatus.

triggers.grounds: Low is the right band and the reason given is true and specific. Re-derived from the bytes: MT 2:15 opens אֶֽחֱזוּ (oshb:Song.2.15, tier: byte), a 2mp imperative, and closes on a 1cp possessive; it carries no dodi/rayati anchor, no daughters vocative, and no form marking the SPEAKER's gender, so the speaker genuinely cannot be settled from this verse. The isolation is warranted on both sides: MT 2:10-2:14 is a quoted 2fs invitation (2fs imperatives and 2fs suffixes throughout) and MT 2:16 opens her mutual-belonging refrain, so the plural-imperative addressee is disjoint from both. Both digits re-sweep exactly: the bare vineyard form כֶּ֣רֶם sweeps to 1 verse (MT 8:11) while the plural and suffixed spellings standing in MT 2:15 escape that sweep on final-mem versus medial-mem allography, and the blossom token סְמָדַֽר (oshb:Song.2.15) sweeps to 3 verses (MT 2:13, MT 2:15, MT 7:13 = WEB 7:12), the dual arithmetically right. The straddling blossom link is disclosed and correctly tier-labelled: סְמָדַ֖ר (oshb:Song.2.13) against oshb:Song.2.15 collates at skeleton tier only. The MT 2:13 ketiv/qere is disclosed with no reading claimed, and the front-seam setumah at MT 2:14 is in the WLC inventory and carried as single-witness tier-3 corroboration. frontier_flag_considered is true. Confidence is not over-stated and is not masking a defective warrant.

findings.claim: device_notes narrates the authoring process and the staging apparatus instead of the text.
findings.grounds: The uncertainty disclosure says the speaker is unmarked by any tier-1 form available in the staged extract, and that this is a bespoke hold rather than a boilerplate one. Both describe the pipeline and the drafting requirement rather than the verse: bespoke-versus-boilerplate is authoring-process vocabulary and the staged extract names the staging apparatus. The binding register law is that row prose describes the TEXT, never the process. Purely cosmetic -- the substantive claim behind it is byte-true, since MT 2:15 carries no speaker-marking gendered form (אֶֽחֱזוּ, oshb:Song.2.15, tier: byte, marks a masculine-plural ADDRESSEE, not the speaker).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair in device_notes: state the hold in text register -- MT 2:15 carries no speaker-marking gendered form, no dodi/rayati anchor and no daughters vocative -- and drop both the staged-extract phrase and the bespoke/boilerplate clause.

triggers.grounds: The band itself is honest and both outer edges are byte-warranted, so it is neither over- nor under-stated. Front edge: מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (oshb:Song.3.6) collates byte at its own ref and byte against oshb:Song.8.5, and the ascent-run formula re-sweeps to exactly 2 verses (MT 3:6, MT 8:5) -- the row's sweep-2-verses-at-byte-tier citation is exact. Back edge: MT 4:1 opens the rayati-bound formula argued in the following row. The closing vocative splice צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Song.3.11, tier: byte) is byte-exact and its digit re-sweeps to 1 verse for the daughters-of-Zion form (the daughters-of-Jerusalem substring sweep returns 7 verses only because it catches the MT 3:10 from-phrase, which the row correctly does not count as an address). The three setumot disclosed (MT 3:5 front-seam, MT 3:8, MT 3:11) are all in the WLC inventory, all carried single-witness tier-3, none used as a driver, and the disclosure sweep is complete for the span. The stated reason for the band -- that lyric_address is a closest-fit rather than a literal address-form match across MT 3:6-3:10 -- is true and is properly disclosed in device_notes; frontier_flag_considered is true. The row's real weakness is a field defect recorded separately below, not a mis-set confidence band.

findings.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative carries no rival boundary at all -- it rejects two unit_type labels -- so this six-verse span ships without engagement of any rival cut, including one its own prose points at.
findings.grounds: The field rejects forcing the span into wasf_poem or narrative_sequence as a worse fit than lyric_address, and says the span is argued into lyric_address by the closest-fit operative category with the deviation disclosed below. That is a unit_type justification, and the book's operative-category law routes exactly that disclosure to device_notes, where this row already carries it -- so the rival-boundary slot is spent on a duplicate. A rival cut was available from the row's own bytes: MT 3:7-3:10 carry no first- or second-person address form at all (verified -- every suffix across those four verses is third-person), and MT 3:11 then opens צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Song.3.11, tier: byte), two 2fp imperatives plus the book's only daughters-of-Zion vocative (sweep: 1 verse), which under the book's voice policy is tier-1 voice-shift evidence standing exactly at the 3:10|3:11 junction. The row's own device_notes concedes the point by saying the addressee shift to the daughters of Zion only surfaces at the closing imperative in Song.3.11, and separately discloses a span-internal setumah at MT 3:8 (single-witness tier-3, correctly non-driving) at the other candidate joint. I am NOT concluding that the shipped span is wrong -- the maximal-run rule and the processional coherence support holding MT 3:6-3:11 whole -- only that the strongest available rival is unengaged, which is a warrant gap on a medium_low row. Not alone load-bearing: both outer edges stand on byte-verified tier-1 anchors. Noted inside the same sentence and folded into this finding rather than scored separately: the phrase closest-fit operative category imports governance vocabulary into row prose.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the unit_type sentence with an actual rival-cut engagement -- reject, or accept and re-span, the 3:10|3:11 cut at the daughters-of-Zion vocative onset, quoting the pointed splice at oshb:Song.3.11 with its tier -- and leave the operative-category deviation disclosure where it already stands in device_notes. Any resulting respan is an adjudication question, not this review's proposal.

triggers.grounds: Band is honest. The in-verse case re-derives byte-exact: the possessor shift from her 1cs garden form to the 3ms garden form inside MT 4:16, closed by her word-for-him anchor, with יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל (oshb:Song.4.16, tier: byte) carrying the dodi token itself. Both digits are exact against the byte-swept inventory and both count objects are named: dodi-exact 24 verses, dod-family 28 verses (my independent substring sweep returns 25 verses, the extra being the MT 5:1 dod-family plural -- precisely the blend the row avoids). The absence statement is true: no parashah seg touches MT 4:16, the neighbouring segs being MT 4:11 and MT 5:1, and it is used as disclosure and never as counterevidence. The back seam is tier-1 warranted by the next verse's own bytes, אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ (oshb:Song.5.1, tier: byte), his address vocabulary. frontier_flag_considered is true and the stated reason for the band is bespoke. Separately: the slice carries an EXCL-lane evidence entry for this row's device_notes phrase about only its own reply settling the invitation, but no excl tag was assigned and none is warranted -- that only is modal, with no count object and no frequency claim behind it, so it falls outside the exclusivity class and needs no digit.

findings.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative engages only the backward fold; the stronger rival -- holding MT 4:16 with MT 5:1 as one invitation-and-answer unit -- is conceded in device_notes but never engaged in this row.
findings.grounds: The field rejects folding MT 4:16 into MT 4:8-4:15, a real but weak rival since that span is his voice throughout. The row's own device_notes then concedes the stronger one, that the invitation only its own reply can settle and that the reply belongs to the verse immediately following. The straddling device is byte-true and I collated it: יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל (oshb:Song.4.16, tier: byte) is answered clause-for-clause by בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ ... אָכַ֤לְתִּי (oshb:Song.5.1, tier: byte), and under the book's closed vocabulary a verse-scale invitation-and-answer pair is an available dialogue_exchange reading, so this is a rival to the row's granularity and not only to its edge. The cross-seam cohesion rule makes a straddling byte-true device argue continuity against the row unless disclosed; the disclosure here is general and unspliced, and the byte-quoted rebuttal lives in the adjacent row rather than in this one. Severity held at low because the seam itself is tier-1 warranted by אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ (oshb:Song.5.1, tier: byte) and the seam partner does carry the rebuttal.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: make the strongest_rejected_alternative the 4:16-plus-5:1 hold, rejecting it on the address-vocabulary shift at oshb:Song.5.1 with the straddling clause pair spliced and tier-labelled, and move the backward fold to the optional second sentence if it is retained.

triggers.grounds: Well calibrated, and every load-bearing claim re-derives. The closing bracket is exactly what the row says it is: אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת collates BYTE at oshb:Song.6.4 and BYTE at oshb:Song.6.10 in both directions, and the byte sweep returns exactly 2 verses (MT 6:4, MT 6:10) -- the identical-byte-tier-phrase claim is true at the tier named. The opener carries a genuine tier-1 rayati vocative with the 2fs pronoun, and the 2fs body-part forms the row lists at MT 6:5, MT 6:6 and MT 6:7 all stand in those verses; the mechanically derived body-part run is indeed confined to MT 6:5-6:7 (3 verses), which the row states rather than conceals. Count-object discipline on the mi-zot family is exemplary and re-sweeps exactly: the bare interrogative returns 3 verses (MT 3:6, MT 6:10, MT 8:5) while the ascent-run formula returns 2 (MT 3:6, MT 8:5, byte-identical to each other), and the row refuses to blend them -- that refusal is the substance of its rejected alternative. The secondary recurrence is correctly down-tiered: בָּרָ֥ה (oshb:Song.6.9) against oshb:Song.6.10 collates accent_stripped, matching בָּרָה֙ only once cantillation is stripped, and the row says accent_stripped tier only. All three setumot cited (MT 6:3 front-seam in the refs, MT 6:9 span-internal, MT 6:10 back edge) are in the WLC inventory under the right type, single-witness, corroboration only. Both WEB quotations are verbatim with in-field web: refs. The stated reason for the band -- the unmarked internal MT 6:7|6:8 join, which the row says its confidence reflects rather than resolves -- is honest, and the span reaches past the book's own pre-registered 6:4-9 wasf question on a byte-tier bracket rather than on assumption, with the wasf_poem label over three non-wasf closing verses disclosed. No whole-chapter cap applies (7 verses of a 13-verse chapter). No lean on the tier-4 WEB speaker headings anywhere: the only heading in range sits before WEB 6:4 and the row argues that verse from rayati and the 2fs pronoun instead. Nothing found to record on this row.
